title: Your avatar and where it is shown
summary: Your R.E.P.O. avatar is built from named parts and drawn in more than one place: the game keeps a version of you for the world, one for making your icon, and one for your expressions.
body: The avatar is built from parts. The game names its pieces separately, including a left arm, a right arm and the eyelids, so a cosmetic can be laid over one piece instead of over the whole character.
The look is tracked as its own thing. The avatar visuals have their own part of the game, which is why changing how you look stays separate from changing how you play.

You are drawn more than once. The avatar menu carries three separate versions of you: one for the world, one used to make your icon and one for expressions, so the menu is showing different models rather than one.
Your cosmetics are collected together. The game keeps a player's cosmetics as a set, and that set is what the avatar menu and the token machine both work from.
Nothing stays stuck on once you own it. A cosmetic can be hidden again, so the game keeps a condition for whether a piece is shown rather than only a list of what you have collected.
The avatar can also talk. There is a talking animation of its own, which is why the character moves while you are speaking instead of standing still.

What this entry does not tell you: how many cosmetics exist, exactly what the menu shows, or whether the other players see the same thing you do. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The avatar is built from named parts, including a left arm, a right arm and the eyelids.
The avatar's visuals are tracked as their own part of the game.
The avatar menu carries three separate avatars: one for the world, one for icons and one for expressions.
A player's cosmetics are kept together as a set.
A cosmetic can be hidden again after it is unlocked.
The avatar has a talking animation of its own.
Cosmetic objects in the world and cosmetic tokens have their own interfaces.
